reference.source: ESC/ERS Guidelines for Pulmonary Hypertension / Sherlock's Diseases of the Liver and Biliary System
clinicalPearls: A group 1 pulmonary arterial hypertension occurring in the setting of portal hypertension, with or without underlying chronic liver disease

Diagnosis requires pre-capillary haemodynamics at right heart catheterisation (raised mean pulmonary artery pressure and pulmonary vascular resistance with a normal wedge pressure) together with documented portal hypertension

The volume overload and hyperdynamic circulation of cirrhosis can raise pulmonary pressures without truly raising resistance, so resistance must be measured to distinguish true PoPH from a high-flow state
Often asymptomatic early and detected on pre-transplant echocardiographic screening; later causes exertional breathlessness and fatigue
Severity is important for liver transplant candidacy, as uncontrolled pulmonary hypertension markedly increases perioperative mortality
Targeted pulmonary vasodilator therapy can lower pulmonary vascular resistance and may render some patients eligible for transplantation
The severity of portal hypertension does not correlate with the severity of the pulmonary vascular disease
reference.pathophysiology: Portopulmonary hypertension is a pulmonary arteriopathy that develops in patients with portal hypertension. Portosystemic shunting allows vasoactive and proliferative mediators normally cleared or metabolised by the liver to reach the pulmonary circulation, where, together with the high cardiac output and shear stress of the hyperdynamic cirrhotic state, they promote endothelial dysfunction and vascular remodelling. The small pulmonary arteries undergo intimal proliferation, medial hypertrophy, and in situ thrombosis, raising pulmonary vascular resistance in a manner histologically similar to other forms of arterial pulmonary hypertension. The distinction from a simple high-flow state is critical, because volume overload alone raises pressure without raising resistance, whereas established portopulmonary hypertension reflects fixed remodelling that loads and eventually fails the right ventricle.
additionalDifferentials: High-output pulmonary pressure elevation from the hyperdynamic cirrhotic circulation
Volume overload with post-capillary pulmonary hypertension
Idiopathic or heritable pulmonary arterial hypertension
additionalInvestigations: Transthoracic echocardiography as the screening tool for elevated pulmonary pressures, especially before liver transplantation
Right heart catheterisation to confirm pre-capillary physiology and distinguish true PoPH from a high-flow state
Assessment of portal hypertension (imaging, endoscopy, or hepatic venous pressure measurement)
Liver function and synthetic tests with assessment of chronic liver disease severity
Ventilation-perfusion scan to exclude chronic thromboembolic disease
Cardiopulmonary exercise testing and six-minute walk distance for functional assessment
redFlags: Severe pulmonary hypertension in a transplant candidate, which greatly increases perioperative mortality
Syncope or signs of right heart failure indicating advanced disease
Rapid deterioration in exercise tolerance or breathlessness
Pulmonary oedema after vasodilator initiation, prompting reassessment of the haemodynamic profile
reference.prognosis: Prognosis depends on both the severity of the pulmonary vascular disease and the underlying liver disease; untreated moderate to severe disease carries a poor outlook. Targeted therapy can improve haemodynamics and, in selected patients, restore eligibility for liver transplantation, after which the pulmonary hypertension may stabilise or improve.
pitfalls: Diagnosing pulmonary hypertension from pressure alone without measuring pulmonary vascular resistance, thereby confusing a high-flow state with true PoPH
Proceeding to liver transplantation without adequately treating significant pulmonary hypertension
Confusing portopulmonary hypertension with hepatopulmonary syndrome, which has opposite vascular physiology
Assuming pulmonary severity tracks liver severity when the two are independent
Overlooking screening echocardiography in cirrhotic patients being assessed for transplant
references: ESC/ERS Guidelines for the Diagnosis and Treatment of Pulmonary Hypertension
